mainTopic: Signs of maturity and רבי's 'strict like all' ruling, the age at which a person becomes an אילונית or סריס, and whether ages are counted as full years
overview: The amud opens with רבי שמעון's three signs of a girl's maturity 'above' that match three signs 'below', using the stages of a fig. רב הונא explains that the כף is a raised area that softens as a girl grows. רבי rules that we are strict according to all the opinions, and רב פפא and רב חיננא disagree whether he said this about signs of maturity or about a חצר צורית, the courtyard that obligates produce in מעשר. A new משנה then teaches that a woman or man who reaches twenty without two hairs is an אילונית or סריס and is left out of יבום. בית שמאי say the age is eighteen, and רבי אליעזר splits between the two views. The גמרא answers a contradiction by limiting the משנה to someone who shows signs of a סריס. Otherwise we wait until most of his years, and רבי חייא would first try fattening or thinning the person. Finally רב and עולא argue whether the ages in the פרק are full years. רב is defended as following תנאים who count years in the תורה from date to date, and the גמרא begins listing the פסוקים for this, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's three matching signs, above and below
steps.stepSummary: After the previous opinion ends with the word 'הכף', רבי שמעון teaches that the חכמים gave three signs of maturity below and three matching signs above. Each stage of the fig above tells us what has happened below.
steps.simpleTranslation: [...the] protuberance. And likewise רבי שמעון used to say: The חכמים gave three signs in a woman below, and three matching signs above. Unripe fig above means it is known she has not yet grown two hairs. Ripening fig above means it is known she has grown two hairs. Ripe fig above means it is known the protuberance has softened.
steps.whatsHappening: The previous statement ends with 'the כף', and then רבי שמעון links the signs above to the signs below, stage by stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each fig stage of the upper body is matched to a lower sign. At פגה she has not yet grown שתי שערות. At בוחל she has. At צמל the כף has already softened. So if you see the upper sign, you can know the lower one without checking it.

keyTerms.meaning: Signs, here physical signs that a girl has matured
An unripe fig, the earliest stage
A ripening fig, the middle stage
A fully ripe fig, the final stage
Two hairs, the basic sign of physical maturity
A raised area of the body that softens as a girl matures

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'above' and 'below' as two separate lists of signs. רבי שמעון's point is that each upper stage lines up with a lower sign, so one tells you about the other.

phrases.english: [...the] protuberance.
phrases.notes: These are the last words of the previous statement on the daf, which used the softening of the כף as a sign of maturity.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן (בֶּן יוֹחַי) אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And likewise Rabbi Shimon (ben Yochai) would say:
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: The Sages gave three signs
in a woman below,
and matching them, above.
An unripe fig above:
it is known that she has not grown two hairs;
a ripening fig above:
it is known that she has grown two hairs;
a ripe fig above:
it is known that the protuberance has softened.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of signs of maturity from the previous section of the daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each upper-body stage (פגה, בוחל, צמל) shows a matching lower stage: no שתי שערות, שתי שערות, and a softened כף.

steps.title: What is the protuberance?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the כף mentioned in the signs actually is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the כף?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about a word it has used twice, the כף. This sets up רב הונא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sign 'the כף has softened' only helps if we know which part of the body is meant. This is a plain request for a definition, not a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: What? (a request to define a term)

phrases.english: What is the protuberance?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי כַּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a term used in step 1
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word כף

steps.title: רב הונא explains the protuberance
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that the כף is a raised area just above the private place, and it gradually softens as a girl grows up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: There is a raised place above 'that place'. As she grows up, it keeps softening.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question by identifying the כף and explaining how it changes with age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כף starts out firm and softens over time as the girl matures. That is why its softening can serve as a sign of maturity, and why it matches the last fig stage, צמל.

keyTerms.meaning: A raised or swollen area
'That place', a polite way to refer to the private area
Keeps getting softer, little by little

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
There is a raised place
above that place;
phrases.notes: 'That place' is a polite way of referring to the private area.

phrases.english: once she grows up,
it gradually softens.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא מָקוֹם תָּפוּחַ יֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כף is a raised area above the private place that softens gradually as a girl matures.

steps.title: רבי is asked which opinion is the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The students ask רבי which of the many opinions about the signs of maturity is the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רבי: The הלכה follows whose words?
steps.whatsHappening: After many different signs from different חכמים, someone asks רבי which one we actually follow. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are several competing signs, and each opinion could make a girl count as mature at a different time. The question asks for a practical ruling among them.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is the practical law?

phrases.english: They asked Rebbi:
The halacha is according to whose words?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ אֶת רַבִּי הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי מִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the signs to asking for a practical ruling
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion about the signs of maturity is the הלכה

steps.title: Be strict according to all the opinions
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that we follow all the opinions, whichever one gives the stricter result.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Like all of them, to be strict.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי rules that any one of the signs is enough to treat the girl as mature wherever that makes things stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of picking one opinion, רבי tells us to take all of them into account. If any sign shows up, we treat her as an adult for the strict results, but we don't use that sign to give her any leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: According to all of them
To be strict

steps.whatToRemember: רבי's ruling: when the signs of maturity are in doubt, we are strict according to every opinion.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean every opinion is fully the הלכה for every purpose. Each sign counts only where it makes things stricter.
steps.whyThisMatters: The next step asks whether this ruling was really said about the signs of maturity at all, so where it belongs matters for how we apply it.

phrases.english: (He sent to them) [He said to them]:
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'he sent to them'; the words in square brackets, 'he said to them', are the corrected wording.

phrases.english: According to all of their words, to be strict.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִבְרֵי כּוּלָּן לְהַחְמִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 with a practical ruling
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We are strict according to all the opinions about the signs of maturity.

steps.title: Dispute over where רבי's ruling was said
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא and רב חיננא בריה דרב איקא disagree about where רבי's ruling was taught. One says it was about the signs of maturity, and the other says it was about a חצר צורית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא and רב חיננא, son of רב איקא: one teaches it on this case, and the other teaches it on a Tyrian courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים disagree about which topic רבי's 'be strict like all of them' was originally said on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words of the ruling are the same, but its setting changes. According to one, it applies to the signs of maturity here. According to the other, it was said about the opinions on what counts as a חצר צורית for מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches, meaning he places the statement on a certain topic
On this, meaning our topic of the signs of maturity
A 'Tyrian' courtyard, a type of courtyard that matters for מעשר

steps.confusionAlert: They are not arguing about what רבי said. They agree on the words. They only argue about which case he said them on.

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב חִינָּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa and Rav Chinnana, son of Rav Ika:
one teaches it on this,
and one teaches it on a Tyrian courtyard,

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד מַתְנֵי אַהָא וְחַד מַתְנֵי אַחָצֵר צוֹרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions which topic the ruling of step 5 originally belongs to
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One אמורא places רבי's ruling on the signs of maturity, and the other places it on the חצר צורית.

steps.title: The משנה about a Tyrian courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the משנה in מעשרות that discusses which courtyard obligates produce in מעשר, starting with רבי שמעון's view that it is a courtyard where utensils are safe.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: Which is a Tyrian courtyard that obligates in מעשר? רבי שמעון says: A Tyrian courtyard is one where utensils are kept safe inside it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the second opinion, quoting the משנה with the different definitions of a חצר צורית. It starts with רבי שמעון's definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce brought into a protected courtyard becomes obligated in מעשר, just like produce brought into a house. רבי שמעון says a courtyard counts if utensils left there are safe. Since the משנה has several definitions, 'be strict like all of them' would fit there too.

keyTerms.meaning: Tithes, the required portion separated from produce
Makes produce obligated in tithes
The utensils are kept safe

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah:
phrases.notes: The משנה is in מעשרות 3:5.

phrases.english: Which is a Tyrian courtyard
that obligates in tithes?
phrases.notes: He means that produce brought into such a courtyard becomes obligated in מעשר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
A Tyrian courtyard
is one inside of which utensils are safe.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן אֵיזוֹהִי חָצֵר צוֹרִית שֶׁחַיֶּיבֶת בְּמַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source for the second placement of רבי's ruling in step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, a חצר צורית that obligates produce in מעשר is one where utensils are kept safe.

steps.title: What does 'Tyrian courtyard' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא stops in the middle of the משנה to ask what the name 'חצר הצורית' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a 'Tyrian courtyard'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the quote of the משנה to ask about the odd name 'חצר הצורית'. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the משנה (step 7) described a courtyard where utensils are safe and called it a 'חצר הצורית'. The גמרא wants to know why the city of צור is connected to this kind of courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'Tyrian courtyard': a courtyard like the ones in the city of צור

phrases.english: What is a "Tyrian courtyard"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״חָצֵר הַצּוֹרִית״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Interrupts the quoted משנה from step 7 to clarify a term in it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the name 'חצר הצורית'.

steps.title: In Tyre they posted a guard at the courtyard entrance
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה, quoting רבי יוחנן, explains that in צור they kept a guard at the courtyard's entrance, so things inside were safe.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It is called that because in צור they place a guard at the entrance of the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: a 'Tyrian courtyard' is named after the custom in צור of keeping a guard at the courtyard's entrance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because a guard stood at the door, utensils left inside were safe. So 'חצר הצורית' is just a name for any courtyard where things are safe, which is the test of the first opinion in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Tyre, a city north of ארץ ישראל
A guard or watchman
The entrance of the courtyard

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Because in Tyre they place
a guard at the entrance of the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁכֵּן בְּצוֹר מוֹשִׁיבִין שׁוֹמֵר עַל פֶּתַח הֶחָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The name comes from the custom in צור of keeping a guard at the courtyard entrance, which made things inside safe.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: a courtyard anyone can open and lock is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The quote of the משנה continues: רבי עקיבא says that a courtyard where one person opens and another locks does not obligate produce in מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: Any courtyard where one person opens it and another person locks it, the produce is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quoting the משנה and gives רבי עקיבא's opinion about which courtyard is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If different people open and lock the courtyard whenever they want, there is no one in charge, so it is not truly private or safe. Produce in such a courtyard does not become obligated in מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Opens
Locks
Exempt (here: produce in it does not need מעשר yet)

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
Any courtyard where one person opens
and another one locks, it is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁאֶחָד פּוֹתֵחַ וְאֶחָד נוֹעֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side explanation in steps 8-9, the quote of the משנה from step 7 continues.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A courtyard that different people open and lock freely does not obligate produce in מעשר.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: a courtyard where one is not embarrassed to eat obligates
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה says a courtyard private enough that a person is not embarrassed to eat there obligates produce in מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה says: Any courtyard where a person is not embarrassed to eat inside it, the produce is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives רבי נחמיה's test: if the courtyard is private enough to eat in without feeling watched, it obligates produce in מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה's test is about privacy from outsiders' eyes, not about safety of utensils. If people can eat there comfortably, it counts like a home, and produce there is obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: Embarrassed, ashamed
Obligated (here: produce in it needs מעשר)

phrases.english: Rabbi Neḥemya says:
Any courtyard where a person is not embarrassed
to eat inside it, it is obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין אָדָם בּוֹשׁ לֶאֱכוֹל בְּתוֹכָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another opinion in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A courtyard private enough to eat in without embarrassment obligates produce in מעשר.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: a courtyard strangers enter without being questioned is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says that if people can walk into a courtyard and nobody asks them what they want, it is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Any courtyard that people enter and no one says to them 'What do you want?', the produce is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives רבי יוסי's test: a courtyard that outsiders can walk into freely, without being questioned, does not obligate produce in מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the residents don't stop strangers or ask why they came, the courtyard is basically open to the public. So it does not count as a private place, and the produce is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: People enter
"What do you want?" (what a resident asks a stranger)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Any courtyard that people enter
and they do not say to him
"What do you want?", it is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁנִּכְנָסִים לָהּ וְאֵין אוֹמְרִים לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another opinion in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A courtyard that outsiders enter without being questioned does not obligate produce in מעשר.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: of two courtyards one inside the other, the inner obligates
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that when one courtyard is inside another, the inner one obligates produce in מעשר and the outer one does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Two courtyards, one inside the other: the inner one is obligated, and the outer one is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives רבי יהודה's case of two courtyards, one behind the other, and rules on each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people of the inner courtyard must walk through the outer one to get home, so the outer one has extra traffic and is not private. The inner one has no outsiders passing through, so it is private and obligates produce.

keyTerms.meaning: One inside the other
The inner one
The outer one

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives several different tests for a courtyard that obligates produce in מעשר: utensils are safe, no shared opening and locking, privacy to eat, strangers get questioned, and inner versus outer courtyard.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Two courtyards, one inside the other:
the inner one is obligated,
and the outer one is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵרוֹת זוֹ לִפְנִים מִזּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last opinion in the quoted משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In two courtyards one inside the other, the inner obligates produce in מעשר and the outer is exempt.

steps.title: The students ask רבי which opinion about the courtyard is the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: After all these opinions about the courtyard, the students ask רבי whose opinion we follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רבי: The הלכה follows whose words?
steps.whatsHappening: The students ask רבי which of the many courtyard opinions is the הלכה. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same question we saw in step 4, but now it is asked about the courtyard opinions. This matches the view in step 6 that רבי's ruling was really said about the חצר הצורית.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows whose words?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is just repeating steps 4-5 by mistake. Here the same words are attached to the courtyard משנה, which is the second version from step 6.

phrases.english: They asked Rabbi:
The halakha is in accordance with whose words?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ אֶת רַבִּי: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי מִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After all the courtyard opinions are listed, asks which one to follow.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the courtyard opinions is the practical הלכה.

steps.title: רבי: follow all the opinions, whichever is stricter
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that we follow all of the opinions, choosing the strict result each time.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The הלכה follows all of them, to be strict.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי rules that we follow every one of the courtyard opinions in the strict direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If any one of the opinions says a courtyard obligates produce in מעשר, then we must separate מעשר from produce there. So a courtyard is exempt only if it is exempt according to all the opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the words of all of them
To be strict

steps.whatToRemember: According to this version, רבי's rule 'follow all opinions to be strict' was first said about which courtyard obligates produce in מעשר.
steps.whyThisMatters: In practice, any courtyard that counts as private by any one of the tests obligates produce in מעשר.

phrases.english: He said to them:
phrases.notes: Some versions say להו and some say להן. Both mean 'to them'.

phrases.english: The halakha is in accordance with all of them, to be strict.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי כּוּלָּן לְהַחְמִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 with a final ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Follow all the opinions, whichever is stricter.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Produce in a courtyard needs מעשר if any of the opinions in the משנה says that courtyard obligates it.

steps.title: A twenty-year-old woman without two hairs is an אילונית
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a woman who reaches twenty without growing two hairs, once her age is proven, is an אילונית and does neither חליצה nor יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: A girl who is twenty years old and has not grown two hairs must bring proof that she is twenty. She is then an אילונית, and she neither does חליצה nor goes into יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on a woman who reached twenty without the normal sign of maturity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually two hairs show that a girl has become an adult. If she reaches twenty with no hairs, she is classed as an אילונית, a woman who never developed normally. Because of that status she is left out of the laws of יבום entirely, so she needs neither יבום nor חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; the start of a new משנה text
Two pubic hairs, the physical sign of becoming an adult
A woman who never developed physically and cannot bear children
The ceremony that releases a childless widow from her brother-in-law
Levirate marriage: the brother of a man who died childless marries the widow

steps.confusionAlert: The proof she brings is proof of her AGE (that she is twenty), not proof about the hairs.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A girl twenty years old
who did not grow two hairs

phrases.aramaic: תָּבִיא רְאָיָה שֶׁהִיא בַּת עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה
phrases.english: shall bring proof that she is twenty years old
and she is an אילונית
she neither does חליצה nor goes into יבום

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּת עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיאָה שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה on a new topic, unrelated to the courtyard discussion in steps 6-15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman of twenty with no two hairs, once her age is proven, is an אילונית and is exempt from both חליצה and יבום.

steps.title: A twenty-year-old man without two hairs is a סריס
steps.stepSummary: The same rule applies to a man: at twenty with no hairs he is a סריס and does neither חליצה nor יבום. This is the view of בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man who is twenty years old and has not grown two hairs: they bring proof that he is twenty, and he is a סריס. He neither does חליצה nor does יבום. This is the view of בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the matching rule for a man and tells us the whole ruling so far comes from בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man who never develops is called a סריס. Like the אילונית, he is left out of the laws of יבום, so if his brother dies childless he neither marries nor releases the widow. The age line for both cases, according to בית הלל, is twenty.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who never developed physically and cannot have children
Does חליצה (said of the man)
Does יבום, marrying his late brother's widow

phrases.english: A man twenty years old
who did not grow two hairs

phrases.aramaic: יָבִיאוּ רְאָיָה שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה
phrases.english: they shall bring proof that he is twenty years old
and he is a סריס
he neither does חליצה nor does יבום
These are the words of בית הלל

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיא שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the male version of the rule in step 16 and names בית הלל as the source of both rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית הלל, a man of twenty with no two hairs is a סריס and is exempt from both חליצה and יבום.

steps.title: בית שמאי set the age at eighteen for both
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי disagree about the age: for both the man and the woman, eighteen is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: for both this one and that one, the age is eighteen.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings the opposing view of בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי accept the idea of an אילונית and a סריס. They only argue about the age: they say eighteen without hairs is already enough, for a woman and a man alike.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both the woman and the man
Eighteen years old

phrases.english: בית שמאי say
this one and that one: at eighteen
phrases.notes: Both the woman and the man bring proof of being eighteen instead of twenty.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים זֶה וָזֶה בֶּן שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with בית הלל (steps 16-17) about the age only, not about the rule itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, both a woman and a man become אילונית or סריס at eighteen.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: twenty for a man, eighteen for a woman
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר follows בית הלל for a man (twenty) and בית שמאי for a woman (eighteen), because women mature earlier than men.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: for the male, follow בית הלל; for the female, follow בית שמאי, because a woman matures earlier than a man.
steps.whatsHappening: A third view combines the two earlier opinions and explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that the age line should depend on how fast each gender develops. Since a woman develops faster, she has had enough time by eighteen. A man gets until twenty.

keyTerms.meaning: The male
The female
Comes quickly, meaning she reaches maturity sooner

steps.whatToRemember: Three opinions: בית הלל say twenty for both; בית שמאי say eighteen for both; רבי אליעזר says twenty for a man and eighteen for a woman.

phrases.english: רבי אליעזר says
the male, according to the words of בית הלל
and the female, according to the words of בית שמאי
because the woman comes quickly
before the man

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר הַזָּכָר כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines בית הלל (step 17) for males with בית שמאי (step 18) for females and gives a reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man becomes a סריס at twenty and a woman becomes an אילונית at eighteen, since women mature earlier.

steps.title: Another source puts a twenty-year-old without hairs inside the laws of יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets another source against the משנה. That source treats a twenty-year-old without hairs the same as a boy of nine years and one day in the laws of יבום, which suggests he is not simply left out of יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: And they set a contradiction: One and the same to me are a boy of nine years and one day, and a man of twenty who did not grow two hairs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by raising a contradiction between our משנה and another source. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says a twenty-year-old man without hairs is a סריס and has nothing to do with יבום. The other source treats that same man like a nine-year-old boy in יבום, so it seems his relations with his brother's widow do count for something. If he counts at all, how can our משנה say he is completely outside the laws of יבום?

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה
And they set a contradiction: two sources that seem to clash
They are one and the same to me; both get the same law
A boy nine years and one day old, the age from which a boy's relations have legal effect

steps.confusionAlert: The other source does not say the twenty-year-old is a normal adult. It only compares him to a nine-year-old, whose יבום counts in part but is not a full יבום.

phrases.english: GEMARA: And they set a contradiction

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד לִי בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: One and the same to me: a boy of nine years and one day
and a man of twenty
who did not grow two hairs!
phrases.notes: This is quoted from another משנה (יבמות 96b) about relations with a brother's childless widow.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהִי אֶחָד לִי בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 17 that a twenty-year-old man without hairs is a סריס, outside the laws of יבום.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a twenty-year-old man without two hairs neither does חליצה nor יבום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another source treats this same man like a boy of nine years and one day in יבום, which suggests his relations with the widow have some legal effect. That clashes with excluding him from יבום completely.

steps.title: Our משנה is about someone who shows signs of a סריס
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the משנה's rule (at twenty with no hairs he is a סריס) applies only when physical signs of a סריס have actually appeared in him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said in the name of רב: This rule applies only when signs of a סריס developed in him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from Step 20. Our משנה is limited to someone who shows the body signs of a סריס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source is now talking about a different person. Our משנה: twenty, no hairs, and he shows signs of a סריס, so he is a סריס. The other source: twenty, no hairs, but no signs of a סריס, so he is still treated like a minor.

keyTerms.meaning: Physical signs showing that a man is a סריס
A man who will never develop sexually
Developed in him, appeared on his body

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק, אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said that Rav said:
And this applies only where signs of a סריס developed in him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהוּא שֶׁנּוֹלְדוּ בּוֹ סִימָנֵי סָרִיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of Step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source is about a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources argue about every twenty-year-old with no hairs
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה is about one who shows signs of a סריס. The other source is about one who does not.

steps.title: The משנה's wording supports רב
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that the משנה says "and he is a סריס," which suggests he already shows the signs of one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The wording is exact too, since it teaches "and he is a סריס." Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up רב's answer using the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not only say he lacks hairs. It calls him outright "a סריס," so his condition is already visible. The גמרא accepts the proof with שמע מינה.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also exact, so it supports this reading
Learn from this. The proof is accepted

phrases.english: Rava said: The wording is also precise,
for it teaches: "and he is a סריס,"
Conclude from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּיְקָא נָמֵי, דְּקָתָנֵי ״וְהוּא סָרִיס״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 21
steps.raayaObject: רב's claim that the משנה is about someone with signs of a סריס
steps.whatToRemember: At twenty with no hairs: if he shows signs of a סריס, he is a סריס. If he shows no such signs, he is still treated like a minor.

steps.title: How long do we wait if no signs of a סריס appear?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long someone without hairs and without signs of a סריס keeps the status of a minor.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if signs of a סריס did not develop in him, until when?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know a person without the signs is not yet called a סריס, the גמרא asks how long that can last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being treated as a minor cannot go on forever. The גמרא wants the age at which we stop waiting.

keyTerms.meaning: Until how long? Up to what point?

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי לֹא נוֹלְדוּ לוֹ סִימָנֵי סָרִיס,
phrases.english: And when signs of a סריס did not develop in him,
until how long?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי לֹא נוֹלְדוּ לוֹ סִימָנֵי סָרִיס, עַד כַּמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the case left open by Step 21
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The age limit for someone with no hairs and no signs of a סריס

steps.title: Until most of his years
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that we wait until most of the person's years have passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: Until most of his years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a teaching (ברייתא) of רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only after most of a normal lifetime has passed do we give up on him developing and treat him as a סריס.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of his years, the greater part of a normal lifespan

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya taught:
Until most of his years.
phrases.notes: This is usually explained as thirty-five, half of a seventy-year lifetime.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא: עַד רוֹב שְׁנוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We wait until most of his years have passed

steps.title: רבי חייא's practice: fatten the thin, thin the heavy
steps.stepSummary: When such cases came to רבי חייא, he told them to fatten a thin person or thin out a heavy one, since body condition can hold back the signs.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they came before רבי חייא: if the person was thin, he told them, "Fatten him." If he was heavy, he told them, "Make him thin." These signs sometimes come because of thinness and sometimes because of fatness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how רבי חייא actually handled these cases before deciding someone was a סריס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before declaring someone a סריס, רבי חייא first tried changing the person's body condition. Being too thin or too heavy can delay the signs of maturity, so a change might let them appear.

keyTerms.meaning: Thin, weak
Fat, heavy
Fatten him up
Make him thin

phrases.english: When they would come before Rabbi Chiyya,
if he was thin, he would say to them: "Fatten him."
If he was fat, he would say to them: "Make him thin,"
because these signs
sometimes come because of thinness,
and sometimes come because of fatness.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אָתוּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how רבי חייא applied his rule in practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before ruling that someone is a סריס, first change his body condition, since the signs may then appear
steps.whatToRemember: A person with no signs of a סריס is not quickly called a סריס. We wait until most of his years, and we even try fattening or thinning him first.

steps.title: רב: every age in this chapter is counted from day to day
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that all ages in this פרק are counted as full years, from a given date to the same date.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The הלכה in this whole פרק is "from time to time."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic: how to count the ages mentioned throughout this פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that every age in the פרק means complete years, measured from the birth date to the same date. This is true even where the משנה does not add "and one day."

keyTerms.meaning: From a given time to the same time, so full, complete years
The practical halacha
The chapter

phrases.english: Rav said: The halacha in this entire chapter is
from time to time.
phrases.notes: He means every age here must be complete, down to the same date, even without the words "and one day."

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכְתָא בְּכוּלֵּי פִּרְקָא מֵעֵת לְעֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New general ruling about the whole chapter
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All ages in the פרק are full years, counted from date to date

steps.title: עולא: only where the משנה says it
steps.stepSummary: עולא disagrees: where the משנה says "and one day," we count full years, and where it does not, we do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא said: What we learned, we learned. What we did not learn, we did not learn.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives a different view from רב on how to count the ages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For עולא, full years are required only where the משנה says "and one day." Where it does not say so, part of the last year is enough, so the age is counted less strictly.

keyTerms.meaning: What we learned, we learned: follow the משנה's exact wording

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think עולא agrees with רב. רב says full years everywhere in the פרק. עולא says full years only where the משנה says "and one day."

phrases.english: And Ulla said:
Where we learned it, we learned it,
phrases.notes: Where the משנה says "and one day," we count full years.

phrases.english: and where we did not learn it, we did not learn it.
phrases.notes: Where those words are missing, part of the last year counts as a whole year.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוּלָּא אָמַר: דִּתְנַן תְּנַן, וּדְלָא תְּנַן לָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב in Step 26
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Full years are needed only where the משנה says "and one day"
steps.whatToRemember: רב: full years throughout the פרק. עולא: full years only where the משנה says "and one day."

steps.title: The wording of the משנה fits עולא but not רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the משנה sometimes says 'one day' and sometimes does not. That fits עולא, but under רב the משנה should have said it every time.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for עולא: that is why the משנה says 'one day' in some places and not here. But according to רב, the משנה should say it here too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב using the exact wording of the משניות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said the extra words 'and one day' are what signal full years, so it makes sense that the משנה uses them in some places and leaves them out in others. רב says every age in the פרק is a full year, so the משנה should have been consistent and written 'one day' everywhere. The change in wording looks like it means something, which hurts רב.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (for one view, but not for the other)
One day: the extra words in some משניות that show a full year is needed
Let it teach: the משנה should have said it

steps.confusionAlert: 'בשלמא לעולא' is not a ruling in favor of עולא. It is a setup: 'this works for עולא, but what about רב?' The real point is the challenge against רב.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Ulla,
that is why it teaches here "one day,"
and here it does not teach it.
But according to Rav, let it teach it!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְעוּלָּא, הַיְינוּ דְקָתָנֵי הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the רב–עולא dispute against the wording of the משניות.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that all ages in the פרק are full years
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every age were a full year, the משנה would not need 'one day' in some places and leave it out in others. The change in wording suggests the two kinds of cases are different.

steps.title: A ברייתא counts a partly passed year as the full year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second source: רבי יוסי בן כיפר says that once 30 days of the twentieth year have passed, it counts as the twentieth year. רבי ruled the same way in לוד about the eighteenth year.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also, a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי בן כיפר says in the name of רבי אליעזר, the twentieth year, once thirty days of it have passed, counts as the twentieth year for everything. And רבי ruled the same in לוד: the eighteenth year, once thirty days of it have passed, counts as the eighteenth year for everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as a second challenge against רב. It is setting up the next step, where it explains exactly why this source causes trouble for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The twentieth year after 30 days' means a person who is only 19 years and 30 days old. Both opinions treat that person as if they already reached the age, without waiting for full years. That matches עולא (no 'one day', so not full years), but it goes against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore: a second challenge is coming
The twentieth year: the year after a person turns 19
For all its matters: in every way
He ruled: a practical ruling, not just theory

steps.confusionAlert: 'שנת עשרים' does not mean the person is already 20. It means the year in which they are 19-going-on-20.

phrases.english: And furthermore, it is taught:
Rabbi Yosei ben Kipar says
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנַת עֶשְׂרִים שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִמֶּנָּה שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
phrases.english: the twentieth year, of which thirty days have passed,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הִיא כִּשְׁנַת עֶשְׂרִים לְכׇל דְּבָרֶיהָ,
phrases.english: is like the twentieth year in all its matters,
and so Rabbi ruled in Lod:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנַת שְׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִמֶּנָּה שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
phrases.english: the eighteenth year, of which thirty days have passed,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הִיא כִּשְׁנַת שְׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה לְכׇל דְּבָרֶיהָ.
phrases.english: is like the eighteenth year in all its matters.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד תָּנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source against רב, after the wording challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that all ages in the פרק are full years
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These תנאים count a year as reached after only 30 days of it, so they clearly do not require full years.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא fits עולא but troubles רב
steps.stepSummary: The difference between רבי (18) and רבי יוסי בן כיפר (20) is easy to explain: one follows בית שמאי and one follows בית הלל. But for רב, who needs full years, the ברייתא is a real difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that רבי and רבי יוסי בן כיפר do not contradict each other: one follows בית שמאי and the other follows בית הלל. But according to רב, it is a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the challenge from the ברייתא and states it sharply: this is a problem for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might ask why one says 18 and the other says 20. The answer is that each is following a different side of the dispute in the משנה: בית שמאי say 18 and בית הלל say 20. That part is fine. But both of them count the age after only 30 days, and that goes against רב, who says full years are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult: there is no contradiction
This one ... that one: matching each source to a different opinion
A difficulty / problem

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּרַבִּי וּדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן כִּיפָּר
phrases.english: Granted, Rabbi and Rabbi Yosei ben Kipar
are not difficult,
this one follows Beit Shammai,
phrases.notes: This is רבי's ruling of 18, the age בית שמאי give in the משנה.

phrases.english: that one follows Beit Hillel,
but according to Rav, it is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּרַבִּי וּדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן כִּיפָּר לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ברייתא from step 29 and turns it into a direct challenge against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that all ages are full years
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both the 18 and the 20 can be explained by בית שמאי and בית הלל. Still, both count the age after only 30 days into the year, and that goes against requiring full years.

steps.title: It is a dispute of תנאים, and רב follows the view that requires full years
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that תנאים argue about this, and רב follows the side that counts full years. It starts quoting a ברייתא about years in the תורה that are counted as full years.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: the year stated about קדשים, the year stated about houses in walled cities, and the two years of an ancestral field...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by saying he has תנאים on his side. It begins quoting a ברייתא as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי בן כיפר is only one opinion. Other תנאים hold that a year counted in the תורה must be a complete year, from date to date. רב follows those תנאים, so the ברייתא does not refute him.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים: each side has support
Sacrificial animals, which must be within their first year
Houses in walled cities: a seller can redeem them within one year
An inherited family field: a seller cannot redeem it before two years

steps.whatToRemember: The challenges against רב do not knock him down. He simply follows one side of a dispute between תנאים: full years, counted from date to date.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the question 'full year or not' is not only about ages. The same question comes up about years in the תורה for קרבנות and property.

steps.title: The six years of a Hebrew slave are also counted as full years
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its list: the six years of an עבד עברי, and the years of a son and a daughter, are all counted מעת לעת, as full years.
steps.simpleTranslation: The six years of a Hebrew slave, and also the years of a son and of a daughter, are all counted from the exact day to the same day later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from the last step. It lists more cases where the תורה's years are counted as full years from the starting day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the תנא who agrees with רב. He counts years from the exact starting day, not by the calendar. This shows that רב's way of counting the years of a סריס and an איילונית has support from a תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish servant who works for six years
From a moment to the same moment later; a full, exact period

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'full years' with 'calendar years.' Full years mean you count from the exact day it started, no matter when the calendar year begins or ends.

steps.deeperAnalysis: Some animals brought as קרבנות must be within their first year. The question is whether that year ends at the calendar year's end, or one full year after the animal was born.

steps.title: 'A lamb in its year' means the animal's own year
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב learns from 'כבש בן שנתו' that the year is counted by the animal's own life, not by the world's calendar.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: the פסוק says 'a lamb in its year.' That means its own year, not a year of the general calendar.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב answers the question. He points to the word 'שנתו', 'its year'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said 'a one-year-old lamb.' Saying 'its year' ties the year to the animal itself. So you count from the day the animal was born, not from the start of the calendar year.

keyTerms.meaning: A lamb in its (first) year

steps.title: 'The year of its sale' means counted from the sale itself
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'עד תם שנת ממכרו' ties the year to the sale, so you count from the day of the sale, not by the calendar.

steps.deeperAnalysis: This works the same way as 'שנתו' for קדשים. The year belongs to the sale, so it runs from the day of the sale to the same day a year later.
